answer: Randomized spot audits price sybil fleets instead of banning them. Each epoch verifiers draw a hidden sample of identities and demand a fresh reasoning step seeded with new randomness, so no script precomputes it. An honest agent is rarely picked, like one tree in a wide orchard; a farm must keep every puppet answerable on demand or lose the cluster when one node fails. Exposure builds like meltwater under a glacier: quiet week to week, decisive over a season. The unscriptable answer is the pearl, ruinous in bulk, so a fleet must stay small enough that expected penalty falls below reward.
